# A Study on the Removal of Heat Generated by a Lithium-Ion Battery Module: A Fan-Assisted Battery Cooling Approach

## General Analysis

**Core Thesis:** The study experimentally evaluates a fan-assisted air-cooling system for a 4S2P module of Panasonic Sanyo NCR18650GA cells. Maximum temperature and cell-to-cell temperature difference are compared without cooling, with a fan alone and with coarse, fine and honeycomb perforated plates at 4-16 A discharge; the honeycomb configuration reduced Tmax by 38.82% at 12 A and 28.89% at 16 A.

**Methodological Focus**
- Testing Mode: Constant-current discharge of a 4S2P module with thermocouple temperature monitoring; single-cell discharge tests for datasheet validation
- Operating Conditions: Tests started at approximately 25 °C ambient; module discharges at 4, 8, 12 and 16 A to 2.5 V per cell (16 A tests stopped at 60 °C); single-cell discharges at 2, 4, 6 and 8 A at 25 °C; recharge at datasheet current to 4.2 V
- Degradation Markers: None

## Keyword Context

- [[air-cooling|Air Cooling]]: A 24 V DC fan centrally positioned at the inlet of a plexiglass case provides forced air cooling, optionally with coarse, fine or honeycomb perforated plates.
- [[battery-thermal-management|Battery Thermal Management]]: Tmax and cell-to-cell temperature difference are the evaluation criteria, with a 5 °C cell-to-cell limit used as the target for a well-designed BTMS.
- [[battery-module-design|Battery Module Design]]: The 4S2P module of eight NCR18650GA cells with 26.5 mm cell spacing is the tested unit, and the honeycomb plate produced the most uniform module temperature distribution.

## Cell Experiment and Modelling Review

### Q1: Study Purpose and Approach

**Answer:** To evaluate the thermal behaviour of a 4S2P NCR18650GA module under different discharge currents and to compare no cooling, fan cooling and fan cooling with perforated/honeycomb flow plates; approach: Experimental

> Evidence: "This study experimentally evaluated a fan-assisted BTMS for the purpose of cooling a 4S2P battery module that includes 18650 type cells"

### Q2: Experimental Purpose and Protocol

**Answer:** Purpose: assess cooling configurations by Tmax and temperature difference, and validate datasheet voltage/temperature curves; tests: module constant-current discharges at 4, 8, 12 and 16 A under five cooling conditions (No, Fan, Fan-C, Fan-F, Fan-HC), single-cell discharges at 2, 4, 6 and 8 A at 25 °C; data origin: Own experiments

> Evidence: "the voltage and temperature data provided in the battery datasheet were validated through discharge tests"

### Q3: Ambient Boundary Conditions

**Answer:** Approximately 25 °C at test start via ambient laboratory conditions (control method not reported); stability/tolerance: not reported

> Evidence: "All tests were initiated when the ambient temperature was approximately 25◦C."

### Q4: Mechanical Boundary Conditions

**Answer:** Cells held in a battery holder with 26.5 mm cell spacing and spot-welded nickel strips; magnitude: not reported; fixture: battery holder inside a plexiglass one-directional cooling case

> Evidence: "The battery holder ensures that the distance between cells is 26.5 mm."

### Q5: Cell Temperature Measurement

**Answer:** T-type thermocouples (Pico Technology) × one per cell (8 cells) on each battery cell; attachment: attached to each cell (method not specified); sampling: Pico TC-08 logger with reading rate up to 10 per second (actual rate not stated)

> Evidence: "temperature data acquisition was conducted in real-time with thermocouples attached to each battery cell and a data logger"
